title: A frame for the story nights, chosen from captures of the real thing
tier_reason: p1 of P-15; the first version ships without a frame on purpose, and the frame is a taste call that needs the real overnight on screen to judge.
ask: Once the overnight player (the Jade item) is on main: render three frame treatments over real captures of the crow night and the robot night — a postcard (rounded card, thin light border, the Day-N type beneath), a viewfinder (corner brackets, a faint scan line; the near-future edge the studio allows), and a dream (a soft cloud-edged vignette, since it is a sleep) — every colour from the shipped palette, nothing smoothed. Also render 'no frame' as the fourth, since that is what ships. Put them to Daniel as one lettered decision card in hq/data/decisions/ with the captures attached and a recommendation, per the studio's rule that visual picks are shown as captures of the real game before he is asked. Do not build the winner; that is a follow-up for Jade.
first_action: Wait for the overnight player to land, then capture a crow night with a display.
source_message: Filed from the 2026-09-10 brainstorm on where the Animation Lab loops enter play (P-15, Q-103, Q-104).
result:
Done. The overnight player was already on main, so I captured both story nights from the real running game and drew the frames over those captures.

**What I made.** Two tools: `tools/capture_overnight_plates.tscn` photographs the sleep mid-play on both story nights — the crows gorging, the seeder robot — by staging each night's own conditions and sleeping through the real gateway, and `tools/compose_overnight_frames.py` draws the candidates over those photographs without needing a display. Eight sheets are in `docs/design/mockups/overnight_frames/`, one per treatment per night, and they hang off a new decision card, **Q-106**, with the queue entry and a recommendation. I did not build any of it into the game.

**What the frames are.** Every colour is one the game already uses — the frames add exactly two, the dirt base and the accent teal from the style guide — and nothing is blurred anywhere: the postcard's corners step on the picture's own pixels, and both soft edges are the same ordered dither the sleep already uses to dissolve an animation's canvas edge into the night.

**My recommendation is the dream** — the picture keeps its middle and dissolves into the night along a wandering cloud edge. It costs no size, adds no colour, and it is the only one of the four that makes the seeder robot's hard ground edge go away instead of pointing at it.

**Three things worth knowing, all of which only showed up by doing it rather than describing it.**

The crow gorge has no room for a card. It is 128×96 on an 800×600 screen, so it plays at ×6 — sixteen pixels short of the screen on each side. A border with the Day-N type beneath costs that night a whole step of size, down to ×5. The sheets show the smaller picture honestly rather than pretending the card is free.

A hard border argues with a dissolving edge. The robot's ground band is dithered into the sky precisely so the ground has no line at the bottom of its canvas — and the postcard's border draws that line back one pixel further out.

And a real bug, not mine: **the Day-N card is off-centre.** Its top-left corner is pinned to the middle of the screen instead of its middle, so "Day 2" sits 32 pixels right and 20 pixels low. It has been shipping that way. Jade's layer; filed below.

Both test suites are green (2666 and 878), the gateway and front-end checks pass, and the writing check reports nothing on any of the new text. One small tidy came with it: taking the documented crow-night shot used to leave two untracked files behind every time, so the ignore rule now covers their sidecars the way the workbench captures' does.

conversation.text: Chief of staff: applied by hand. Your patch collided with Dmitri's on the queue and design/09 because both seats opened a Q-106 in the same hour; the frame keeps Q-106 and the sound pick is Q-107. Two corrections from the check, made in the card, the queue and design/09: the dither band runs down a loop's left and right edges only, so the robot's ground already ends in a hard line at the bottom and a border repeats that line rather than crossing a dissolve (the recommendation stands, on that truer ground); and the p0 paragraph now says the crow plays at ×6, matching the code. The off-centre Day-N card you found is fixed in the same commit (the label is now full-rect with centred text), so no item goes to Jade for it.

follow_ups.title: Draw the picked frame around the animation the sleep plays
follow_ups.first_action: Read the ruling on hq/data/decisions/Q-106.json, then implement that frame in systems/day_cycle.gd around the overnight loop sprite; tools/compose_overnight_frames.py holds the exact geometry and colours each candidate was drawn with (padding, border and corner radius in loop-pixel cells, the dither matrix, the two palette entries). Keep the loop's whole-number scale rule, and if the postcard was picked, step the crow gorge down to x5 as the sheets do. Add a case to tools/test_runner.gd asserting the frame is present during loop_playing and absent on a plain night.
follow_ups.why: The card is a pick between four built candidates, so accepting it is choosing which one goes into the sleep.

recommend.question: Which of the four frames goes around the picture the sleep plays?
recommend.answer: The dream — the picture keeps its middle and dissolves into the night along a wandering cloud edge.
recommend.why: It is the only one that makes the seeder robot's hard ground edge disappear instead of drawing attention to it, and it costs no size and adds no colour.
recommend.instead: No frame, which is what ships today — the crow night already looks right without one, and the robot's ground edge could be fixed in the animation instead.

check.summary: The four frames are drawn over real captures of both story nights and sit on a Q-106 card with a recommendation, but the card and the design doc argue from a wrong fact about where the robot's ground dissolves, and the doc now says the crow loop plays at both ×5 and ×6.

findings.what: The card's argument against the postcard rests on a dissolve that does not exist at the bottom edge: the game dithers a loop's left and right canvas edges only (day_cycle._dither_edge_band), and the no-frame robot capture shows a hard straight line under the ground. The card's own option (a) says so, contradicting its question text, the reply, and the new paragraph in design/09.
findings.fix: Reword both: the robot's ground already ends in a hard line at the bottom; the sides dissolve. The dream is the only candidate that removes that bottom line, which still supports the recommendation, and the postcard adds a second line beneath the first rather than 'drawing the dissolve back'. Note the dither code comment cites design/09 as saying 'left and right', so the p0 paragraph's 'that edge'

findings.what: Design doc contradicts the code and itself: the p0 paragraph still says the crow gorge plays at ×5, while the code picks ×6 on the 800×600 viewport and the new p1 paragraph says ×6.
findings.fix: Change the p0 line to ×6 in the same change, so the doc has one number that matches _build_loop_sprite.

findings.what: The green-suite, gateway, front-end and writing-check claims could not be re-run from this seat (every shell command was blocked), so the 2666 and 878 figures are the worker's word, not verified here.
findings.fix: Run both suites and the three checkers before committing, per the drain rule that nothing lands on the worker's own report.

findings.what: The Day-N off-centre bug is real and correctly diagnosed: set_anchors_preset(PRESET_CENTER) pins the label's top-left to screen centre, and the captured card shows 'Day 2' starting at the centre point rather than straddling it. Not a defect of this diff, but the follow-up item for Jade is sound.
